title: Sketching Graphs of Quadratic Functions
seo_title: Sec 3 Sketching quadratic graphs Worksheets: Free Secondary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: sketching the graphs of quadratic functions given in the form y = (x − p)² + q, y = −(x − p)² + q, y = (x − a)(x − b) and y = −(x − a)(x − b); solving quadratic equations by the graphical method
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 maths worksheets on sketching quadratic graphs: turning points, maximum and minimum values, intercepts, lines of symmetry and solving equations by the graphical method. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: y = (x − p)² + q has its turning point at (p, q).
key_sub: y = (x − a)(x − b) cuts the x-axis at a and b; a minus sign in front turns the graph upside down.
body_html:
How it works

  • y = (x − p)² + q is ∪-shaped with a minimum point (p, q). y = −(x − p)² + q is ∩-shaped with a maximum point (p, q).
  • y = (x − a)(x − b) cuts the x-axis at x = a and x = b. The line of symmetry is halfway between them.
  • The y-intercept is the value of y when x = 0.
  • To solve f(x) = k from a graph, read the x-values where the curve meets the line y = k.
Example

Sketch y = (x − 2)² − 9.

Minimum point (2, −9)

x = 0 gives y = −5

y = 0 gives x − 2 = ±3, so x = −1 or 5

Answer: ∪-shaped through (−1, 0), (5, 0) and (0, −5)

Example

Find the maximum point of y = −(x + 1)(x − 5).

Roots −1 and 5, so the line of symmetry is x = 2

y = −(3)(−3) = 9

Answer: (2, 9)

Common mistakes

  • Taking the turning point of y = (x − 3)² + 1 as (−3, 1). It is (3, 1).
  • Calling the turning point of −(x − p)² + q a minimum. The minus sign makes it a maximum.
  • Reading the roots of (x − 2)(x + 4) as 2 and 4. They are 2 and −4.
  • Reading the y-values instead of the x-values when solving from a graph.

faq.q: How do you find the turning point of y = (x − p)² + q?
faq.a: The turning point is (p, q). It is a minimum if the square is positive and a maximum if there is a minus sign in front of the square.

faq.q: How do you sketch y = (x − a)(x − b)?
faq.a: Mark where it cuts the x-axis at x = a and x = b, find the y-intercept by putting x = 0, and draw a smooth ∪ (or ∩ for a minus sign) symmetrical about x = (a + b)/2.

faq.q: What is the line of symmetry of a quadratic graph?
faq.a: A vertical line through the turning point, x = p for y = (x − p)² + q, or x = (a + b)/2 for y = (x − a)(x − b).

faq.q: How do I solve an equation using a graph?
faq.a: Draw the curve and the line y = k. The x-coordinates of the points where they meet are the solutions of f(x) = k.
